# Rung L, rung-label-exit: label and exit on the compiled path

- problem: the code generator had no case for a label block or an exit, 'Can't compile Label', so every declaration that holds one was refused, the one library's `Indexed.indexOf` among them (ledger row 81): `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2189`
- spec: "Label and Exit": `Specification/basic/expressions/label.tex:12`
- precedent: walk's `forLabel` and `forExit`, an exit as a thrown Java object that the label's handler takes: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:628`
- deviation: walk matches an exit to a label by the label's name, and gives 104 where the compiled exit, which names one evaluation of the label block as fork L1 asks, gives 102 (`compiler_tests/LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled`): `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1793`
- deviation: walk's `try` offers an exit to its `catch` clauses as the library's `LabelException`; no compiled `catch` clause takes an exit, as the specification has it: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:1453`
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1776`

One launch worked this rung. Base c1ce2a35e1; the Java of the rung is commit 3accd77d82 and did not change after it; the later commits add tests and these files.

## What changed and why

`CodeGen.java` gets two members directly above `defaultCase` (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1776-1857`), and the runtime one class, `runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java`.

- `forLabel` (`CodeGen.java:1793`) makes a new `LabelExit.Target` for each evaluation of the block and keeps it in an immutable local under the label's name. The body is compiled in a nested scope that holds that local. An exception-table entry for `LabelExit`, written after the body's code so that the entries of a label, a `try` or an `atomic` block nested in the body come first, leads to a handler that calls `LabelExit.valueAt(target)`: it answers the exit's value where the exit names this evaluation and throws every other exit on. The value is cast to the label's type.
- `forExit` (`CodeGen.java:1838`) evaluates the `with` value, or pushes `()`, loads the target's local, and throws `LabelExit.of(value, target)`.
- `LabelExit` (`runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java:14`) is a Java `Error` that is no `FException`, without a stack trace. `LabelExit.Target` (`:19`) is an `FValue`, so that a closure holds it as it holds any immutable variable.

How an exit reaches its label from a loop's body. The body of a `for` is a function expression, and an arm of a parallel group a task; each takes the variables of the enclosing block that its body names from `FreeVariables`, in which every identifier counts (`compiler/codegen/FreeVariables.java:98`), the target of an exit among them. So the closure's class gets a field for the label's local with no change to `forFnExpr`, `delegate` or `forLetFn`. The checker lets no variable in scope share a label's name ('Cannot use an existing identifier … for a 'label' expression', `scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:704`), so the name is free in the code generator's environment of locals. The exit thrown in the closure passes the library's code, and a group of forked arms joins the arms that it forked before it throws the exit on (`CodeGen.joinForkedArms`, `CodeGen.java:1657`; P-175).

## The failing run and the passing run

Failing, on the base's code, before the first build of the edit (the run ended 2026-11-17 00:32:18 UTC):

    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh base ProjectFortress/compiler_tests LabelExitCompiled.test ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.test

    . link ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled
     UNEXPECTED exception
    com.sun.fortress.exceptions.CompilerError:
    ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled.fss:13:29-20:10:
        Can't compile Label at ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled.fss:13.29
    Tests run: 4,  Failures: 3,  Errors: 0

Passing, the last run after the last change of code, at four threads (head 9e67d603d0's tests on 3accd77d82's code):

    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh final ProjectFortress/compiler_tests LabelExitCompiled.test ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.test XXXLabelNumeralValueCompiled.test AtomicBlockLaterArgumentLink.test XXXAtomicBlockLaterArgument.test FinallyOnEscapeLink.test XXXFinallyOnEscape.test

    . run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled (661ms) PASS
    OK (9 tests)

and, after the test of an evaluation's identity got its own file, the same list with `LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled.test` and `ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled.test` (`junit.sh final2 …`):

    . run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled (674ms) PASS
    . run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled (466ms) PASS
    OK (13 tests)

At one thread and at four, directly (`cd ProjectFortress && ../bin/fortress compile compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled.fss`, then `FORTRESS_THREADS=1 ../bin/fortress run LabelExitCompiled` and `FORTRESS_THREADS=4 …`; the same for `LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled`): `PASS`, exit 0, each.

The whole compiled suite, once, on commit 3accd77d82 (`ant testFast`): `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, `Total time: 8 minutes 35 seconds`; the four tracks' result files sum to 2444 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.

The walk tests: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-label-exit/h1 ProjectFortress/tests/XXXExitThroughCatchWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`: `OK Saw expected exception` twice, `OK (2 tests)`.

The first expected-failure test, shown red on a deliberate fix: with `exit done` of `XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.fss` replaced by `()` for one run, `junit.sh red … ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.test` printed `REACHED`, `PASS`, `Did not see expected failure`, `Tests run: 2,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0`; the file was then restored.

## Each form tested (`compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled.fss`, and `LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled.fss` for the identity)

Failing on the base as above, passing after at one thread and at four:

- an exit with a value out of a `while` (`outOfWhile`), and the same `while` that no exit leaves;
- an exit without a value (`noValue`), and an exit without a target (`noTarget`);
- an exit out of a `for` over a range (`outOfFor`): the label's value is one of the values that an iteration exits with; a loop that one iteration exits; a loop that none exits;
- a label nested in a label, the inner exit naming the outer or the inner (`nested`);
- a label as a function's whole body with three exits (`severalExits`);
- an exit inside a `try` whose `catch` takes every exception, which does not take it, beside a `throw` that it takes (`throughTry`);
- an exit out of a function expression called by another function (`outOfFunction`);
- the identity of an evaluation, in a test of its own because the paths differ on it: in a recursive function, the exit of a function expression made at depth 2 and called at depth 0 leaves the evaluation at depth 2, 102 and not the 104 that matching by name gives and walk prints (`descend` of `LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled`);
- the form of the library's `indexOf`: a method of a generic trait whose `for` exits with a `Just` beside a block that ends in a `Nothing` (`Holder.indexOf`), and with an index (`Holder.find`);
- an exit out of the first arm of a `do … also do` (`outOfArm`); a label and its exit inside one `atomic` block, whose writes stay (`insideAtomic`).

## Where the fix belongs, and the precedent search

The map's row for the feature (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md`, "Feature by feature", `label` / `exit`) gives the checker's cases (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:700`, `:731`), walk's members, and for the code generator "no `forLabel`, no `forExit`". The disambiguator gives every exit its target and its `with` expression (`scala_src/disambiguator/ExprDisambiguator.scala:513`), and the checker types the label, so the code generator is the only place that lacked the construct.

Precedents followed, all in `CodeGen.java`: the handler whose table entry is written after the code that it covers, at three sites, `forAtomicBlock` (`:1937`), `forTry` (`:2256`) and `joinForkedArms` (`:1685`); `forThrow` (`:2227`) for an expression that ends in `ATHROW`; `forLocalVarDecl` and `bindAndGenerateClauseBody` for a local in a nested scope. No earlier change repaired this defect elsewhere.

Names added, and the grep for a competing declaration over both test corpora and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/`: `LabelExit`, `LabelExit.Target`, `LABEL_EXIT`, `LABEL_EXIT_TARGET` have none; `forLabel` and `forExit` are the visitor's methods, which `CodeGen` did not override; walk's classes are `exceptions/LabelException.java` and `NamedLabelException.java`. The new tests' names have no other file. No `.test` file pinned 'Can't compile Label' or 'Can't compile Exit' (`grep -rl` over `ProjectFortress/*tests/`: nothing).

## What the specification settles

- A label's value is its body's, or the `with` value of an exit that names it; an exit without a `with` clause has `()` (`label.tex:52-66`). Built.
- The `finally` clauses of the `try` expressions between an exit and its label run, innermost first (`label.tex:72-76`). Not built: the compiled `try` runs its `finally` clause only on the paths that row 890 names.
- A group of implicit threads completes abruptly when one of its threads does, and every thread of the group has then not run, completed or been stopped early (`evaluation/parallelism.tex:86-93`). Built by the landed join of forked arms.
- An exit out of an `atomic` block retains the block's writes (`atomic.tex:60-63`). Not built: see the points.
- The specification says nothing of an exit that runs after its label block has completed, and names no `LabelException` (`grep -rn LabelException Specification/ --include=*.tex`: nothing).

## Programs run old against new

None was run on the base's code beside the failing harness run above; the base's refusal is row 81's record. The ladder subset, after the edit only: the one file of the baseline whose recorded first error names the construct, `tests/objectCC_label.fss` (`explorations/compile-ladder/baseline-2026-09-19/ladder.tsv:314`: `codegen`, 'Can't compile Label at …objectCC_label.fss:123.18'). With the drivers copied under `tmp/rung-label-exit/ladder/` (`bash run-subset.sh`): `tests/objectCC_label.fss crc=1`, still at the code generator, its first error now the next wall, 'Can't compile ObjectExpr at …objectCC_label.fss:125.23'. No file moved down. The gate does not run this file.

## Sentences of the specification made false

None. No Effect of Appendix I and no note names a missing label or exit on the compiled path (`grep -n -i 'KWD{label}\|KWD{exit}' Specification/appendices/changes.tex` gives only the entry on expected types, lines 2508-2567, which speaks of the checker and stays true).

## Points to report reached

1. **exit as built.** A thrown `LabelExit` that names one evaluation of its label block (`CodeGen.java:1838-1857`, `:1793-1836`).
   - From a loop's body, a closure that can run in a task: the closure holds the evaluation's identity as a captured immutable variable; the exit passes the library's loop and each group's join. Shown at four threads by `outOfFor`, `Holder.find` and `Holder.indexOf` of the test.
   - The other iterations of a parallel loop: an arm that was forked runs to its end or to its own exit before the label takes the exit, and an arm that was never forked does not run. A probe that exits at `i = 900` of `0#1000` and counts bodies under `atomic`: at one thread `value 900, bodies run 901`, six times; at four threads `value 900, bodies run 1000`, six times. A probe in which every seventh iteration exits (`i MOD 7 = 3` of `0#1000`): at four threads `value 3` eight times, with 909 to 926 bodies run. The value is that of the first arm, in the arms' order, that exited, as `joinForkedArms` gives for exceptions; the test asserts only that it is one of the exiting values.
   - A `finally` clause between the exit and its label does not run: `throughFinally(1)` of a probe printed `1` and `log []` compiled, at one thread and at four, and `log [finally]` only where no exit left the `try`. Not built; the case is in `compiler_tests/XXXFinallyOnEscape.fss` (`exits`), row 890.
   - An exit out of an `atomic` block: not built. `compiler_tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled` (with `ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test`) is the expected failure, `FAIL:  0 =/= 7`; new row NEW-L-1. Walk loses the writes too (`tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`, `0 =/= 7`).
2. **Each form tested**, failing on the base and passing after at one thread and at four: the list above.
3. **Every existing test whose pinned message changed:** none. Two existing expected-failure programs of the revival gained a case each and stay expected failures: `compiler_tests/XXXAtomicBlockLaterArgument.fss` (`left`, and the comment line) and `compiler_tests/XXXFinallyOnEscape.fss` (`exits`, and the comment line). The `VerifyError` of the first now names its method `left`.
4. **The distance stage's shadow patch** still applies: `python3 explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/shadow-patch.py ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress tmp/rung-label-exit/shadow` printed 'shadow sources written to tmp/rung-label-exit/shadow', exit 0, on 3accd77d82's `CodeGen.java`.
5. **Sentences of the specification made false:** none.
6. **Files edited, for STAGE_BLIND:** `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java`; tests `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled.{fss,test}`, `LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled.{fss,test}`, `ExitOutOfAtomicCompiledLink.test`, `XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled.{fss,test}`, `XXXLabelNumeralValueCompiled.{fss,test}`, `ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled.{fss,test}`, `XXXAtomicBlockLaterArgument.fss`, `XXXFinallyOnEscape.fss`, `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`, `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXExitThroughCatchWalk.fss`. Neither stage ran: the section asks for none. **Beyond those named:** the two walk tests under `ProjectFortress/tests/`, and the two existing compiled test programs; no source file beyond the two named.
7. **Reserved points.** A model line: none. A change to a class name that a test or the class loader reads: none; the rung adds the classes `LabelExit` and `LabelExit$Target`, and a field named after the label in a closure or task class whose body exits, and renames nothing.

## Decisions

1. **An exit is a thrown Java object that its label's handler takes.** Ways not taken: a jump inside the method for an exit that stands in its label's own method, which needs the operand stack and the handlers between the two known and leaves a second mechanism for a closure; a table of live labels per task, which a forked task does not see. Evidence: walk's `forExit` and `forLabel`; fork L1.
2. **The identity of an evaluation is a new object in an immutable local under the label's name.** Ways not taken: walk's match by name, under which `descend(4, …)` gives 104 for 102, and which the letter of `label.tex:61-66` also allows (question 4); a static identity by the label's position, which fails the same recursion; a special argument through `forFnExpr` and `delegate`, which the section keeps out of. Evidence: fork L1; `FreeVariables.java:98`, `Misc.scala:704`; `compiler_tests/LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled`; the same program under walk printed `104`.
3. **`LabelExit` is an `Error` that is no `FException`, has no stack trace, and has no public constructor.** Ways not taken: an `FException` with a Fortress value, which a `catch` of `Exception` would take, as walk's does; a constructor of one `Throwable` or of none, which `ForkJoinTask` uses to copy an exception that it rethrows in another thread, losing the target and the value. Evidence: `forTry` catches `FException` only (`CodeGen.java:2256`); `FException` has one constructor of an `FValue`.
4. **The local's Fortress type is `Any`, and `LabelExit.Target` extends `FValue`.** A captured immutable variable becomes a field and a constructor parameter at its type's JVM descriptor and is cast to it (`CodeGen.constructWithFreeVars`), so the object must be an `Any`. Way not taken: a `LabelType` local, for which `NamingCzar` has no descriptor.
5. **The `with` value is evaluated before anything of the exit is on the operand stack,** and a static `LabelExit.of` makes the object. Way not taken: `forThrow`'s order, `NEW`, `DUP`, then the value, which leaves an uninitialised object under a value whose own code may branch from a handler.
6. **The handler casts the exit's value to the label's type.** Without the cast the verifier joins the body's value with `Object`. A union type is erased by `generalizedCastTo`, and a `Bottom` label is not cast.
7. **An exit out of an `atomic` block is not built.** The way tried on paper: `forExit` commits the transactions between itself and its label before it throws. The block's handler then calls `BaseTask.leaveTransaction`, which takes the task's current transaction, now the block's parent, and ends it (`runtimeSystem/BaseTask.java:293-314`); so it is right only where no transaction encloses the label, and the handler is not this rung's. The section's own default: the expected failure and the row.
8. **A `finally` clause on an exit's way is not built.** A copy of the clauses' code before the throw reaches only a `try` in the exit's own method, not one around a loop whose body exits; `forTry` is not this rung's. The case joins row 890's test.
9. **A label block as a call's later argument is not built.** It fails as an `atomic` block and a `try` do there (row 322): a handler clears the operand stack. The case joins row 322's test.
10. **The test spells each number that a label block yields beside an exit's value as a typed variable.** `PLabel.fss` as the planner wrote it, `exit found with i` beside a last `-1`, does not compile after the rung: the label's type is the union of `ZZ32` and the numeral's type, and its coercion to the declared `ZZ32` crashes the code generator, row 340's 'Error trying to close method scope'. A `POP` on the fall-through of `forTypecase`, tried in a scratch copy of `CodeGen.java`, turns that crash into `VerifyError: Bad return type`, so the repair is not one line and is row 340's. Recorded as `compiler_tests/XXXLabelNumeralValueCompiled`.
11. **An exit that runs after its label block has completed stays an uncaught `LabelExit`,** with the message 'exit from a label block that has completed'. Way not taken: a throw of the library's `LabelException`, which walk's `try` offers to `catch` clauses; the specification names no such exception, and whether a program may catch it is the curator's (below).

## Defects, each with its home

1. Row 81, the refusal: repaired; home 1, `compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled`.
2. An exit out of an `atomic` block loses the block's writes, on both paths: home 2, `compiler_tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled` and `tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`; new row NEW-L-1.
3. Under walk a `catch` clause of `Exception` takes an exit (`leave(1)` gives 101 for 1): home 2, `tests/XXXExitThroughCatchWalk.fss`; new row NEW-L-2. Walk only; compiled, the test's `throughTry` passes.
4. Compiled, a `finally` clause between an exit and its label does not run: home 2, the case `exits` in `compiler_tests/XXXFinallyOnEscape.fss`; a note on row 890. Walk runs it (`log [caughtfinally]` shows the clause, with defect 3 beside it).
5. Compiled, a label block as a call's argument after the first fails verification, 'Current frame's stack size doesn't match stackmap': home 2, the case `left` in `compiler_tests/XXXAtomicBlockLaterArgument.fss`; row 322 rewritten. Walk prints 2 and 104 for the probe.
6. Compiled, a label block whose value joins a numeral with a `ZZ32` stops the code generator: home 2, `compiler_tests/XXXLabelNumeralValueCompiled`; row 340 rewritten.
7. An exit that runs after its label block has completed: the specification is silent and the paths differ; home 3, `compiler_tests/ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled` asserts today's compiled behaviour; new row NEW-L-3.

8. The paths differ on which evaluation of a label block an exit leaves where the block is evaluated again inside itself, 102 compiled and 104 under walk: the rung builds fork L1's answer, and the letter of the specification can be read for walk's; home 3, `compiler_tests/LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled` asserts today's compiled behaviour; new row NEW-L-4.

## Questions for the curator

1. Who builds the exit out of an `atomic` block (NEW-L-1)? The compiled handler and walk both discard the writes; the specification retains them (`atomic.tex:60-63`).
2. Is an exit that passes a `try` a `LabelException` that a `catch` clause may take, as walk's `try` has it (`Evaluator.java:1453-1456`) and both libraries declare, or no exception, as `label.tex` reads and the compiled path now does (NEW-L-2, NEW-L-3)?
3. The natural spelling of a search, `exit found with i` beside a last `-1`, waits for row 340.
4. Which evaluation does an exit leave where its label block is being evaluated more than once (NEW-L-4)? Fork L1 gives each evaluation its own identity, and the rung built that: the exit leaves the evaluation in which its function was made. Walk takes the innermost running evaluation of that name. The specification scopes the target statically (`label.tex:39-46`), and also says that a label expression completes normally where its body completes abruptly with an exit whose target is its name (`label.tex:61-66`), which is true of the innermost evaluation's body.

## Commands worked out

- The ladder subset of one file: the drivers of `gate.md`, "The ladder regression", copied to `tmp/rung-label-exit/ladder/`, with `printf 'tests\tobjectCC_label.fss\n' > subset.txt` and the two copies of `default_repository/caches` under `root/`.

# Writing a test

**gated test**
: Test that the gate's suites run.

**green**
: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as passed.

**red**
: Harness's report on a test that JUnit counts as failed.

**`XXX` test**
: Gated expected failure. It asserts the answer that the specification gives, and fails today. The harness reports it green while it fails, and red when the defect is fixed.

## A test program

A test program has this form:

    component Name
    export Executable

    (* declarations *)

    run(): () = do
        assert(f(2), 4, "f(2)")
    end

    end

- `(*)` starts a comment to the end of the line. It cannot hold `*)`: the parser ends the comment there and refuses the program. `(* ... *)` comments nest.
- A compiled test with a `run` key ends `run()` with `println("PASS")`, unless a `run_out` key checks its output (below).
- Under walk, `assert(x, y, msg)` checks that `x` equals `y`. It and `=/=` call a type's own `=` only if the type extends a `FortressLibrary` trait that declares `=`, such as `Equality` (ledger row 807). Otherwise they compare by `SEQV` (`revival-changes.md`, "Traits and objects"). If a type `P` has its own `=`, make `P` extend `Equality[\P\]`, or write `assert(x = y, msg)`. The compiler's library declares the two-value `assert` only for `ZZ32`, `String` and `Character`; its `assert(flag, msg)` takes any `Boolean`.
- Do not name a variable or a parameter after a functional method of the library, such as `big`, `even`, `numerator` or `shift`. The disambiguator, the phase that binds names, refuses it: "Variable even is already declared."
- A superscript is `^` and what follows it, as the exponent in `x^2` or the transpose `^T`. It can follow a dotted access: `p.wq^T` is `(p.wq)^T`. After a call or a subscript, parenthesise first, as `(f(x))^T` and `(x[5])^2`: `f(x)^T` is a static error, and `x[5]^2` stops the compile, and under walk fails or gives the wrong element (ledger rows 1005 and 1).
- A test of run-time arithmetic or concatenation needs a variable operand, not a literal, because an expression of literals alone folds before the run (`revival-changes.md`, "Numbers").

## Where a test goes, and how it passes

Interpreter (walk): write `ProjectFortress/tests/Name.fss`, whose component is `Name`.

- Every `.fss` file there is gated, with no `.test` file needed.
- It is green if it throws no exception, exits 0, and neither its standard output nor its standard error contains `fail` or `FAIL`. A longer word counts too: `failure` fails the test. Only a file whose name contains `QuickCheckTest` is exempt.
- An api that it imports, and a helper component, go in `ProjectFortress/test_library/`. In `tests/`, a helper would run as a test.
- The harness skips files whose names end in `Syntax.fss`, `DynamicSemantics.fss` or `Satisfiability.fss`, or contain `GenomeUtil`.
- For a refusal at load, put `Name.test` beside `tests/Name.fss`, with `load_exception_contains=<message>`. A plain test is green if walk refuses the program at load as named. A failure while the top-level variables are initialised counts as a refusal. An `XXX` test here records a refusal that walk misses: it is green while the program loads and runs clean, and red once walk refuses it.

Compiled: write `Name.fss` and `Name.test` in the compiled test folder that holds tests of its kind:

- `library_tests/`: the compiler's library. A test of the interpreter's library is an interpreter test (above).
- `parser_tests/`: the parser.
- `compiler_tests/`: the rest, beside the team's numbered `CompiledN` tests.
- `other_compiler_tests/`: the team's compiled tests that do not fit the `CompiledN` series. Put no new test there.

The `.test` files are the whole list of tests: a `.fss` that no `.test` file names never runs. A `.test` file is a Java property file. It names the commands to run and the checks on their output, as lit's RUN and CHECK lines do:

    tests=Name                 the component(s) it drives; without it, the .test file's own name
    compile | link | typecheck each present command is one JUnit case; link compiles, then links
    run                        run the linked program in a subprocess (bin/fortress run)
    <command>_<stream>_<check>=text
                               command: compile, link or run; stream: out, err or exception;
                               check: contains, does_not_contain, equals, matches,
                               WIcontains (containment with runs of whitespace collapsed)

A `run` fails if the program exits non-zero or a `run_*` check fails. With no `run_out` check, its output must contain `pass` or `PASS`. With `run_exits_nonzero=true`, the run must exit non-zero, as a program whose class fails to load does. The `run_*` checks, and the `PASS` check where no `run_out` check is given, still apply. For example:

    tests=EqualityRung1
    link
    run
    run_out_WIcontains=PASS

## How `XXX` works

- Under walk, an `XXX` test is `tests/XXXName.fss`, whose component is `XXXName`. With no `.test` file, it is green when it fails as a plain test would.
- In the compiled test folders, the `XXX` prefix of a `.test` file's name applies to every command that the file drives: each must fail. So a defect at run time, whose link succeeds, needs two `.test` files ("Writing an `XXX` test").
- An unmet `run_*` check makes a run test red, whatever the prefix.
- The harness reports any link or compile exception of a component whose name contains `XXX` as expected, whatever the `.test` file's name. Only an unmet key of that command makes it red.
- An `XXX` compile test with a `compile_err_contains` key, whose program compiles, reports "Saw wrong failure", which is red.
- A green `XXX` test prints `Saw expected failure` or `OK Saw expected exception`.

## How a defect is recorded

Record every defect that you measure in one of three ways, and say in your report which:

1. Your change repairs it: an assertion in your plain gated test. It needs no `XXX` stage.
2. It is deferred, and the specification settles it: a gated `XXX` test that asserts the specification's answer. Write it in the change that measured the defect, even if a later change will repair it. If walk crashes on the program, still write the `XXX` test, unlike under 3: the harness counts the crash as the expected failure. A deferred defect of a program that the checker accepts and that then fails the JVM's verification (`VerifyError`), linkage or a range check at run time is one of these.
3. It is deferred, and the specification is silent or a conflict leaves it open (`exploring.md`): a test that asserts today's behaviour, and a row in the gap ledger (`records.md`). If no program can observe the defect, or no gated test can pass while it shows, as when walk crashes on the program, write the ledger row only. Its reproducer, the row's cell that names the test, is `none`, and its notes give the command and its output.

If your brief does not let you edit the original tree, say in your report which of the three the defect needs, and write a ledger row for it, whichever it needs. The change that next works there writes the test.

## The order: the test, its failure, the fix, the pass

1. Write the test, with a plain name. Write the essence of the defect as a clean, minimal program, not the shape in which a probe met it.
2. See the test fail through the harness (`harness-one.sh` or `junit.sh`, `tests-running.md`) on the base's code. Do this in a run that ends before you first build or compile your edit. Under walk, do it before you edit a library source that the test reads. If your tree already holds the fix, run the test through the harness on the old code, as `worktrees.md`, "Running the old code", says.
3. Make the fix. See the test pass in your last run after your last change of code.

The test needs no commit of its own. A test that comes with no fix has no failing run: see it pass through the harness.

In your report, quote two to five lines of the failing run, if there is one, and the passing line, each with its command. In an edit of the original tree, put every check into a gated test, never into a one-off script. A task that only measures may use its own script. Assert a value with `assert` in an interpreter test. In a compiled test, assert it with `assert` (above), or print it and check it with a `run_out_equals` key.

An edit of prose in `Specification/` or `Documentation/` has no test. Check it as `specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", says.

## Writing an `XXX` test

In a compiled test folder, name the component `XXXName`, in its file `XXXName.fss` and in its `component` line.

- For a refusal at compile time, write one `XXX` compile test, with `compile` and `compile_err_contains=<the refusal's message>`.
- For a code-generator wall (`compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet"), write `XXXName.test` with `tests=XXXName`, `compile` and `compile_exception_contains=<text of the exception>`.
- For a program that compiles and fails at run time, write two `.test` files over the component:
  - `NameLink.test`, a plain name, with `tests=XXXName` and `link`. It is red if the link reports static errors, but green on an exception.
  - `XXXName.test`, with `tests=XXXName` and `run`, and no `link`. Its run uses the plain file's link, so run the two files in one call of `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`, the plain one first.
  - The program prints `REACHED` in `run()` before the part that fails. The `XXX` file checks it with `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or with `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` if the run dies before `run()` prints. Never use `run_out_contains=PASS`.
  - Example: `compiler_tests/XXXBoxDotSpellingsRungW.test` and `BoxDotSpellingsRungWLink.test`.

Show the first `XXX` test that your change adds, and only the first, working through the harness (`harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`), from its place in a gated test folder. Run it twice:

1. As it is: the harness must report an expected failure.
2. Changed for one run so that the defect does not show, then restored: the harness must report it red. For example, add the missing declaration to the test program, set the expected string to what the run prints, or, in a run-time pair, remove the part that fails.

## Promoting an `XXX` test

If your change fixes a defect that has a gated `XXX` test, the fix turns that test red. To find such a test, search the gap ledger (`records.md`): a row's reproducer names it. Also list the `XXX` files: `git ls-files 'ProjectFortress/*XXX*'`. Then promote it:

1. Before you edit the code, remove the prefix: give the test a plain name by its topic. Rename each file with `git mv` (`committing.md` gives the commit), or with `mv` if the file is not committed yet. Rename each `XXX` name inside: the `component` line, and in a compiled test the `tests=` lines and keys. Change a run-time pair as below.
2. See the plain-named test fail through the harness on the base's code, as "The order", step 2, says.
3. Make the fix and see the test pass.

A run-time pair keeps its three files, renamed without `XXX`. For example, `compiler_tests/NatRtTask` was promoted so in `fd5cb4864`:

- `Name.fss`, with `component Name`. The program asserts its values, then prints `PASS` last.
- `NameLink.test`: `tests=Name` and `link`.
- `Name.test`, in place of `XXXName.test`: `tests=Name`, `link`, `run` and `run_out_contains=PASS`.

## Names, comments, citations

- Name a test by its topic. Give it one comment line that says what it checks, with no pointer to a record.
- Assert each case in one test only. Add a new case to the test that already asserts cases of its kind: `git grep` for the case's name or value finds it. A case that fails today goes in an `XXX` test, since it would turn a plain test red.
- Write an assertion's message as one short line that says what was checked. Put a reason that several assertions share in one comment line above them.
- In a test, cite the specification by file and section or entry, never by line: `opr-overview.tex, subsection "GCD, LCM, and CHOOSE Operators"`. In the library chapters, name the entry too: `basic-integers.tex, section "Integers", opr CHOOSE`.
- If your change breaks a line of a test that the team wrote, respell the line and keep the value that it checks. Keep every assertion. List each line's before and after in your report.
- If your change touches mutable state, a field, an `atomic` block, library code that writes shared state, or the Java of tasks, transactions or the class loader, run its checks at one thread and at four. `harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh` and the suites force four threads. For one thread, run the program directly with the prefix `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` (a compiled program: `compiler.md`, "Running"), and check its exit code and output.
- Under walk, a parallel range of sixteen elements or fewer, as `0#16`, runs its bodies in index order, so a test of parallelism there needs a longer range. For the compiled path, see `compiler.md`, "Traps of the compiled path".

# The base build, seeded worktrees and the old code

**seeding**
: Making a worktree with a copy of the build and caches of a built, clean worktree. `seed-worktree.sh` makes the copy and rewrites the paths in it (`SKILL.md`, "The caches").

**base build**
: Clean worktree at the base, built in place by ant, or seeded. Every other worktree is seeded from it.

**old code**
: Base's code, run from the base build with a private caches folder.

Once the base build is built, run its code only as "Running the old code" says, with a private caches folder outside it. Any other run writes into the caches that every worktree is seeded from.

## Finding or building a base build

- If your brief names a base build, use it.
- If not, look in `git worktree list`. Earlier base builds are at paths such as `/home/user/fortress-base<N>`. A worktree can be your base build if it passes three checks:
  - `git -C <it> rev-parse HEAD` prints your base;
  - `git -C <it> status --porcelain` prints nothing;
  - it holds `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`.
- If no worktree passes them, build one at a path of your own, outside the main tree. It takes about 200 s: start the build and the library order detached, with the `nohup` line of `session.md`, "Long commands". `<base-commit>` is your base: the commit that your brief names, else your tree's `HEAD` when you start. Say so in your report.

      git worktree add --detach <base-build> <base-commit>
      cd <base-build>          # then set up the call as build-and-caches.md says
      ant compileAll
      # then the library order (build-and-caches.md), then this walk run, which warms walk's caches:
      bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
      git status --porcelain   # must print nothing: the seeding script refuses a base build that is not clean

If you check a fix against its old code, use a base build at the commit that the fix starts from. If a brief names the fix's base, the fix starts there. If not, the fix starts from `git merge-base <its branch> main`, or from the parent of its first commit on `main`.

## Seeding a worktree

A build, and a run of `bin/fortress` without a private caches folder, walk's too, write into the caches of the tree that they run in. So build and run only in a tree whose caches no other agent uses. Your brief says where you work. If your work builds or runs code and your brief gives you no tree of your own, seed a worktree of your own instead of building one. Then work only there.

Seeding takes about 3 s and 206 MB of disk. The new worktree runs walk and the compiled path right away, with the library already compiled.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh <base-build> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]

- The script checks out `<branch>`: a local branch, else origin's, else a new branch cut from `<start-point>`, by default the base build's commit. With `-`, it makes a detached worktree at `<start-point>`.
- If the script exits 2, the base build is not built or not clean, and the script made nothing. Then make the worktree with `git worktree add`, build it yourself, and say so in your report.
- If the worktree already exists, the script keeps its branch. If it already has a build, the script keeps that too. `SEED_FORCE=1` replaces it.
- If you start in a worktree that has no build, seed it in place: name it as `<new-worktree>`, and its branch as `<branch>`.
- The script lists the library sources that differ from the base build's commit. Before a compiled run, take for each the step that `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library", gives.
- If the script warns that the copied build is the base's, run `ant compileAll`, then the library order. Without the warning, `ant compileAll` keeps the seeded caches.
- If another agent seeded your worktree, make the script's two lists yourself: `git diff --name-only <base> -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin` for the library sources, and `git diff --name-only <base> -- ProjectFortress/src ProjectFortress/astgen build.xml` for the warning.
- Reuse another tree's build or caches only through this script.

## Running the old code

If your worktree holds an edit and you need the base's behaviour, run the old code instead of reverting your edit. For example, see a test fail, or compare a program's old and new output.

`old-fortress.sh` runs the base build's `bin/fortress`. It sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the base build and `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the private caches folder that you name, over your settings. Name a folder inside your worktree's `tmp/`:

    OLD=explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches compile P.fss     # the compiled path ...
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches run P             # ... then the run
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss             # walk
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches junit <worktree>/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/X.test [Y.test ...]   # compiled .test files, in one JVM

- Any copy of the tool works, because it runs the base build that its first argument names.
- On first use, it fills the private folder with a copy of the base build's caches (36 MB, 0.04 s). Later runs use the same folder.
- Every cache file that a run writes goes to the private folder, and nothing else that it writes under the base build stays. So several agents can run the old code at once.
- Keep your programs outside the base build too, because a program writes its own logs beside it. The tool refuses a private folder inside the base build (exit 2).

To run interpreter tests on the old code, run the base build's `harness-one.sh` with `FORTRESS_HOME` set to the base build:

    FORTRESS_HOME=<base-build> <base-build>/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh \
        <worktree>/tmp/old-harness <worktree>/ProjectFortress/tests/X.fss

The `run` step of a compiled `.test` is a separate `bin/fortress run` process. It inherits `FORTRESS_HOME` and `FORTRESS_CACHES`, and takes its class path from `FORTRESS_CACHES`. If you compose a harness run by hand with `-Dfortress.caches=<folder>`, set `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the same folder. Otherwise the `run` step fails with "Could not load ... Resource not found".

(* An exit leaves its label's block, whose value is the exit's with value or (): out of a while, out of a parallel for, out of a function expression, through a label nested in its target and through a try that catches every exception. label.tex, section "Label and Exit". *)
component LabelExitCompiled
export Executable

var bad: ZZ32 = 0

check(what: String, got: ZZ32, expected: ZZ32): () =
  if got = expected then () else
    bad := bad + 1
    println("FAIL " || what || ": " || got.asString || ", expected " || expected.asString)
  end

outOfWhile(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label found
    none: ZZ32 = -1
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < 10 do
      if i = n then exit found with i end
      i += 1
    end
    none
  end found

noValue(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
  var steps: ZZ32 := 0
  label skip
    steps := steps + 1
    if n > 0 then exit skip end
    steps := steps + 10
  end skip
  steps
end

noTarget(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label only
    if n > 0 then exit with n end
    n
  end only

outOfFor(n: ZZ32, r: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label found
    none: ZZ32 = -1
    for i <- 0#n do
      if i MOD 7 = r then exit found with i end
    end
    none
  end found

nested(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label outer
    ten: ZZ32 = 10
    inner: ZZ32 = label middle
        if n = 1 then exit outer with ten end
        if n = 2 then exit middle with 2 ten end
        3 ten
      end middle
    inner + 1
  end outer

severalExits(n: ZZ32): String = label method
    if n < 0 then exit method with "negative" end
    if n = 0 then exit method with "zero" end
    if n > 100 then
      exit method with "large"
    end
    "small"
  end method

object Boom extends UncheckedException end

throughTry(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
  var caught: ZZ32 := 0
  r: ZZ32 = label out
      try
        if n = 1 then exit out with 5 n end
        if n = 2 then throw Boom end
      catch e
        Exception => caught := caught + 1
      end
      7 + caught
    end out
  r + 100 caught
end

call(f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32, x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = f(x) + 1000

outOfFunction(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label out
    call(fn (x: ZZ32): ZZ32 => if x > 2 then exit out with x else x end, n)
  end out

trait Holder[\T extends Object\]
  item(i: ZZ32): T
  count(): ZZ32
  find(p: T -> Boolean): ZZ32 = label found
      none: ZZ32 = -1
      for i <- 0#count() do
        if p(item(i)) then exit found with i end
      end
      none
    end found
  indexOf(e: T, same: (T, T) -> Boolean): Maybe[\ZZ32\] =
      label found
          for i <- 0#count() do
              if same(item(i), e) then exit found with Just[\ZZ32\](i) end
          end
          NothingObject[\ZZ32\]
      end found
end

isJust(m: Maybe[\ZZ32\]): ZZ32 = if m.isNothing then 0 else 1 end

sameText(a: String, b: String): Boolean = a = b

object Words extends Holder[\String\]
  item(i: ZZ32): String = if i = 5 then "five" else "other" end
  count(): ZZ32 = 20
end

var left: ZZ32 = 0
var right: ZZ32 = 0

outOfArm(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label out
    do
      if n = 1 then exit out with n end
    also do
      atomic do left := left + 1 end
    also do
      atomic do right := right + 1 end
    end
    n + 100
  end out

insideAtomic(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do
  r: ZZ32 = atomic do
    left := 5
    label out
      right := 7
      if n = 1 then exit out with n end
      right := 8
      n + 100
    end out
  end
  r + left + right
end

run(): () = do
  check("an exit with a value out of a while", outOfWhile(3), 3)
  check("a while that no exit leaves", outOfWhile(20), -1)
  check("an exit without a value", noValue(1), 1)
  check("a label that no exit leaves", noValue(0), 11)
  check("an exit without a target", noTarget(4), 4)
  one: ZZ32 = outOfFor(100, 3)
  check("the label's value is a value that an iteration exits with", one MOD 7, 3)
  check("that iteration is one of the loop's", if 0 <= one AND one < 100 then 1 else 0 end, 1)
  check("a for that only one iteration exits", outOfFor(7, 5), 5)
  check("a for that no iteration exits", outOfFor(100, 9), -1)
  check("an inner exit that names the outer label", nested(1), 10)
  check("an exit that names the inner label", nested(2), 21)
  check("nested labels that no exit leaves", nested(3), 31)
  assert(severalExits(-1), "negative", "the first exit of a label that is a function's body")
  assert(severalExits(0), "zero", "the second exit")
  assert(severalExits(500), "large", "the third exit")
  assert(severalExits(5), "small", "no exit")
  check("a catch of every exception does not catch an exit", throughTry(1), 5)
  check("the same try catches a throw", throughTry(2), 108)
  check("the same try completes normally", throughTry(3), 7)
  check("an exit out of a function expression", outOfFunction(5), 5)
  check("a function expression that does not exit", outOfFunction(1), 1001)
  check("an exit out of a loop in a generic trait's method, the form of the library's indexOf", Words.find(fn (s: String): Boolean => s = "five"), 5)
  check("a loop of that method that no iteration exits", Words.find(fn (s: String): Boolean => s = "six"), -1)
  check("an exit with a Just beside a block that ends in a Nothing, as the library's indexOf", isJust(Words.indexOf("five", sameText)), 1)
  check("the same method where no iteration exits", isJust(Words.indexOf("six", sameText)), 0)
  check("an exit out of the first arm of a do with also", outOfArm(1), 1)
  check("the same arms without an exit", outOfArm(2), 102)
  check("a label and its exit inside one atomic block, whose writes stay", insideAtomic(1), 13)
  check("the same block without an exit", insideAtomic(2), 115)
  if bad = 0 then println("PASS") else println("FAIL") end
end

end

# Rung L, rung-label-exit: the record lines

## For FACTS

**The compiled path runs `label` and `exit`: an exit is a thrown `LabelExit` that names one evaluation of its label block, and reaches it from a loop's body and from another task.** `CodeGen.forLabel` keeps a new `LabelExit.Target` in an immutable local under the label's name and takes, in a handler, the exits that name it; `CodeGen.forExit` throws `LabelExit.of(value, target)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1776-1857`, `runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java`). A function expression or a task whose body exits captures the target as it captures any immutable variable, because every identifier counts as a free variable (`compiler/codegen/FreeVariables.java:98`) and the checker lets no variable share a label's name (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Misc.scala:704`). A group of forked arms joins the arms that it forked before the exit passes it: at four threads every forked iteration of a parallel `for` runs to its end or to its own exit, and the label's value is the exit of the first arm in the arms' order; at one thread the iterations after the exit do not run. No `catch` clause takes an exit. What it means for the work: the one library's `Indexed.indexOf` compiles in its own form (the test's `Holder.indexOf`), and row 81's wall is gone. Four limits stand, each with its test: an exit out of an `atomic` block loses the block's writes (NEW-L-1); a `finally` clause on the exit's way does not run (row 890); a label block as a call's later argument fails verification (row 322); a label block whose value joins a numeral with a number stops the code generator (row 340), so a number beside an exit's value is bound to a typed variable first. Test: `compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled`, which fails with 'Can't compile Label' without the two members. Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-label-exit/REPORT.md`, "What changed and why" and "Points to report reached".

## Findings

1. **`label` and `exit` compile.** Holds for an exit in its label's method, in a function expression, in a local closure of a loop's body, in an arm of a `do … also do` and in a task, at one thread and at four. Evidence: `compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled` (the harness at four threads: `. run ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled (661ms) PASS`, `OK (9 tests)`; directly at one thread: `PASS`); `ant testFast` on 3accd77d82: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 2444 tests, 0 failures. Meaning: row 81 closes; the next wall of `tests/objectCC_label.fss` is 'Can't compile ObjectExpr'.
2. **The paths differ on which evaluation of a label block an exit leaves.** Holds where a function with an exit, made in one evaluation of a label block, runs inside a later evaluation of the same block, as in a recursive function. Evidence: `compiler_tests/LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled` gives 102, the evaluation that made the function; the same `descend` under walk printed `104`, the innermost evaluation, matched by name (`interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:636-640`). Meaning: fork L1 chose an identity for each evaluation and the rung built it; the specification's letter can be read for walk's answer, so the row is CONTESTED and the question is the curator's (NEW-L-4).
3. **`PLabel.fss` as the planner wrote it does not compile after the rung:** its last `-1` beside `exit found with i` meets row 340. Evidence: `compiler_tests/XXXLabelNumeralValueCompiled`, 'Error trying to close method scope'. Meaning: the batch's record names that program as the rung's first test; the test spells the number as `none: ZZ32 = -1`.
4. **Walk hands an exit that passes a `try` to the `catch` clauses as the library's `LabelException`** (`interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:1453-1456`). Evidence: `tests/XXXExitThroughCatchWalk.fss`, `101 =/= 1`; a probe caught `LabelException` for an exit run after its label block. Meaning: the two paths differ on what a `catch` of `Exception` around a loop with an exit does; the curator's question 2 of the report.
5. **The distance stage's shadow patch applies** to the rung's `CodeGen.java`: exit 0.

## Revival change

### The change

The team's code generator had no case for a label block or an exit: `CodeGen` declared no `forLabel` and no `forExit`, so the node reached `defaultCase`, which refused the declaration with 'Can't compile Label' (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:1859`, `defaultCase`). Walk runs both, and matches an exit to a label by the label's name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/evaluator/Evaluator.java:628-645`, `:500-519`); its `try` offers an exit that passes it to the `catch` clauses as the library's `LabelException` (`Evaluator.java:1453-1456`).

The tree now compiles both (`CodeGen.java:1776-1857`, `runtimeSystem/LabelExit.java`). A compiled exit leaves the evaluation of the label block in which it was made, also from the body of a `for`, from a function expression and from another task; a parallel loop first joins the iterations that it forked, which run to their end or to their own exit; the label's value is one of the exiting values. No compiled `catch` clause takes an exit. Test: `compiler_tests/LabelExitCompiled`. Where a label block is evaluated again inside itself, a compiled exit leaves the evaluation in which its function was made, and walk's leaves the innermost one: `descend` of `compiler_tests/LabelEvaluationIdentityCompiled` gives 102 compiled and 104 under walk.

A compiled program must still keep to four spellings: bind a number that a label block yields beside an exit's value to a typed variable first, as `none: ZZ32 = -1` (`compiler_tests/XXXLabelNumeralValueCompiled`); bind a label block's value in a statement of its own, not as a call's later argument (`compiler_tests/XXXAtomicBlockLaterArgument`); do not rely on a `finally` clause between an exit and its label (`compiler_tests/XXXFinallyOnEscape`); do not exit out of an `atomic` block and rely on its writes, on either path (`compiler_tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicCompiled`, `tests/XXXExitOutOfAtomicWalk.fss`). A function, a variable and a label in scope may not share a name: the checker refuses 'Cannot use an existing identifier … for a 'label' expression'. An exit that runs after its label block has completed ends a compiled program (`compiler_tests/ExitAfterLabelCompletedCompiled`). The skill's list of constructs that the code generator has no case for names `label` and `exit`, which it now has.

The reason, as evidence: the specification's section "Label and Exit" (`Specification/basic/expressions/label.tex:52-66`); the one library's `Indexed.indexOf` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2189-2195`), above every string and array, was refused; the failing run 'Can't compile Label at …LabelExitCompiled.fss:13.29'.

Ledger row 81; the rehearsal's wall W9; fork L1 of the batch record (an exit leaves through the loop's body as an abrupt completion that names its label, each evaluation with its own identity; a parallel loop joins the arms that it forked first) under P-175; climb batch 31, rung L.

# Setting up, building, the caches, and what to rebuild

**tree**
: Checkout of the repository: the main checkout or a worktree. In a command, `<tree>` is the tree that you work in: the one that your brief names, else the one that your session starts in.

**library order**
: Five compiles that build the compiled path's library into the caches.

**DSL grammar**
: `grammar` declaration in an api, which adds syntax for a domain-specific language.

**parser directory**
: New `fortress<random>rats` folder of 5.8 MB, in which a program that imports a DSL grammar gets a Rats! parser generated when it runs. The run makes it in its JVM's temporary directory and never deletes it.

## Setting up each call

Start every Bash call with these lines. They put you at the tree's root, where this skill's commands start unless they `cd`:

    cd <tree> && mkdir -p tmp
    export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH
    export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD FORTRESS_THREADS=1 TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$PWD/tmp"
    unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS

- If `/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64` or `ant` is missing, run `apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y openjdk-25-jdk-headless ant` first.
- `bin/fortress` takes `FORTRESS_HOME` from the shell whenever it is set. If it names another tree, you run that tree's code. Check it with `echo $FORTRESS_HOME`.
- `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` is unset, because the proxy's trust-store flags in it break ant's JVM forks.

The lines give the settings of `explorations/experiment/env.sh`, with two differences:

- The JVM's temporary directory is your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- They leave out env.sh's removal of old parser directories in `/tmp`, because your runs put theirs in your tree's `tmp/` (below).

If your brief tells you to run `source env.sh` and then to point `TMPDIR` and `JAVA_FLAGS` at `tmp/`, use the lines above. They do the same.

The library and microGPT import no DSL grammar, and of the gated tests only `ProjectFortress/syntax_abstraction_tests/ForUse.fss` does. The ungated tests beside it import one, and so do the APL experiments under `explorations/apl/`.

With the lines above, your runs that import a DSL grammar put their parser directories in `<tree>/tmp/`. Hundreds of them once filled the disk allowance. So:

- When no run of yours is live, remove yours: `rm -rf <tree>/tmp/fortress*rats`.
- Before a long run, check `df -h /`. How to read it: the `cloud-container` skill.

## Two layers of code

The repository holds two layers of code. Different tools build them, at different times, so "compile" means a different thing in each layer.

The implementation is the parser, walk, the compiled checker, the code generator and the runtime. It is the Java and Scala under `ProjectFortress/src/`, with the parser grammars (`parser/*.rats`) and the syntax tree generated from `ProjectFortress/astgen/Fortress.ast`. `ant compileAll` builds it into `ProjectFortress/build/` ("Building", below). `ant compile` is another name for it.

The Fortress code is the library, the tests and the programs: the `.fss` and `.fsi` files. The `fortress` commands run the phases on it and keep the results in the caches:

- Walk runs the phases on each component that a run needs. It needs no `fortress compile`.
- `fortress compile` writes a component's jar. It is for the compiled path's components only: the compiler's library, compiled tests and compiled programs.
- `fortress run` compiles no Fortress source.
- A command reuses an entry if no source that the entry depends on is newer than the entry: its own source, and the `.fsi` files of the apis that it imports, at any depth.

An edit makes stale what was built from it:

- Java or Scala: the classes in `ProjectFortress/build/`. Run `ant compileAll`. The cache entries that the edited code wrote are stale too, and no entry notices it: an entry is compared with its sources, never with the implementation. For example, after a change to a native helper's signature, its old wrapper stays in `nativewrapper_cache/`, and the run links the old signature. For this reason, the build deletes the caches when the implementation changes ("Building").
- A parser grammar: the generated parser, and every entry that it parsed. Run `ant compileAll`.
- A `.fss` or `.fsi` file of the library: the entries of that component, and after an `.fsi` edit, the entries of every component that imports the api. Walk analyses them again by itself. A component of the compiler's library needs a compile, or the library order ("After an edit of the library").
- A test or a program: its own entries. Walk and the harness analyse a walk test again by themselves. Compile a compiled test or program again, or let the harness do it.

## The caches

All the caches are gitignored. A caches folder also holds:

- `environment_cache/`: another cache of walk's.
- `nativewrapper_cache/`: the wrappers for the Java classes that an api imports with `import java`.
- `global.map`: the linker's saved state, an empty map in practice. If it is missing, the linker writes an empty one, also in a private caches folder.
- `implementation.stamp`: the stamp of the build that the caches belong to ("Building", below).

Only these runs read `default_repository/caches`: `fortress compile`, `fortress run`, `fortress junit` (and `junit.sh`), `ant testOnly`, and a direct walk run. These runs use private caches (`-Dfortress.caches` and `FORTRESS_CACHES`), and need neither the library order nor warm caches: `harness-one.sh`, the gate's ladder regression (`gate.md`) and both ant suites. `harness-one.sh` keeps its private cache beside its scratch folder between calls (`tests-running.md`).

## The library order

The first of its compiles, `LibraryBuiltin/AnyType`, holds the top type `Any`, which both libraries share. The other four are the compiler's own. All five take about 100 to 110 s after `ant compileAll`.

Run it only when the caches lack the library's jars, or hold stale ones:

- after a build that printed `Caches <tree>/default_repository/caches started again, empty`, and in a tree whose caches are empty;
- after an edit of a library `.fsi` that the section "After an edit of the library" names.

Otherwise the jars are in place, and a compiled test or program needs no library order. The five commands:

    cd ProjectFortress
    ../bin/fortress compile LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss            # 17 s
    ../bin/fortress compile LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss    # 63 s
    ../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss        # 27 s
    ../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss        # 2 s
    ../bin/fortress compile ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss         # 2 s

Before the first compiled run, check that `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/` holds five jars: `fortress.AnyType.jar`, `fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`, `fortress.CompilerLibrary.jar`, `fortress.CompilerAlgebra.jar` and `CompilerSystem.jar`, which has no prefix. Sometimes all five compiles exit 0 and a jar is missing. The cause is not known.

- If a jar is missing, run the five commands again. Once, this made the jars.
- If a jar is still missing, report it as a defect. Quote the commands, their exit codes and the folder's listing.
- Keep the caches in this case too. Once, emptying them made the jars, but a deletion hides the cause.

## Name resolution

- `fortress.source.path` searches `.` (the current directory) first, then `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin`, `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/test_library`. The first `Foo.fsi` or `Foo.fss` that it finds wins. So a file in the directory that you run from hides the library's file of the same name.
- A component's file name without `.fss` must be the component's name.
- If both libraries use one api name, one of them breaks. For this reason, the compiler's apis have the `Compiler` prefix.
- The top-level `CompilerLibrary/` holds `.fsi`-only stubs, not `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`. `lib/` holds Fortress sources, not jars.
- If paths behave wrongly, read `repository/ProjectProperties.java`. It resolves `FORTRESS_HOME`, `BASEDIR` and the cache paths.

## Building

Run `ant compileAll` from the tree's root. It is the only build: `ProjectFortress/build.xml` is a stub.

- It makes the parser and the syntax tree again only if their sources changed.
- javac compiles only the changed Java files and the files that depend on them. scalac runs only if its inputs changed, and then compiles every Scala file.
- It decides by a stamp whether it deletes the caches. `ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp` is a hash of the built implementation, and each caches folder holds the stamp of the build that filled it. At its end, the build keeps `default_repository/caches` if its stamp equals the new one, and empties it if not. It does not touch a private caches folder. It prints `Caches <folder> kept` or `Caches <folder> started again, empty`. The comment "The caches and the implementation" in `build.xml` gives the rule.
- `ant cleanCache` deletes the caches, whatever their stamp.
- With nothing changed, it takes about 4 s. After an edit, it takes about 25 to 60 s on an idle machine, scalac about 19 s of it, and about 50 to 80 s on a new or cleaned tree. While other agents build, it takes up to about 140 s.
- After a build that started the caches again, yours or a test target's, run the library order before the next compiled run. So each edit of Java or Scala costs about 2 to 3 minutes before a compiled run: the build, then the library order.
- If it fails, fix the error and run the same command again. Clear nothing by hand.

## After an edit of the library

The compiled path sees an edit of its library only when you compile the edited component itself. Compiling your own program never recompiles the library under it.

- If you edited the `.fss` of one of the five library components, and not its `.fsi`: run `fortress compile` on that component only. Programs need no recompile.
- If you edited the `.fsi` of AnyType, CompilerBuiltin, CompilerLibrary or CompilerAlgebra: run the whole library order. Every api depends on these four.
- If you edited `CompilerSystem.fsi`: compile CompilerSystem only.
- If you edited any other file of `Library/` or `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`: it is walk's library. Do nothing: walk reads it again, and compiled programs do not link it yet.

## Symptoms of a skipped step

If you skip the step for your edit, the run shows it:

- After an edit of a body, the run uses the old code and gives no warning.
- After an edit of an api, the run stops with `NoSuchMethodError` or `NoClassDefFoundError` on a library member. Examples: `fortress.CompilerBuiltin.println`, `coerce_ZZ32`, `fortress/CompilerLibrary$GeneratorZZ32`. The run found no library jar and used the bootstrap stubs: old class files of the compiler's library that the build compiles from `ProjectFortress/src/fortress/` into `ProjectFortress/build/fortress/`.

If you see either, do the step now: recompile the component, or run the library order. Do not delete the caches to fix it. A deletion works only because it repeats the library order and every analysis from cold. If something else looks like a stale cache, find its cause before you delete anything.

Two messages look like a skipped step, but usually show a defect:

- A `NoSuchMethodError` on a method of your own program, often with a mangled name such as `\=tag?1??Arrow...`, is a defect of the compiled path. Record it (`tests-writing.md`).
- "Unable to read serialized data for X, recommend you delete the Fortress bytecode cache and relink" is usually a defect of the code generator. Search the gap ledger for the message. Run the library order only if X is a member of a `Compiler*` or `AnyType` component. Keep the caches, whatever the message advises.

Two more facts help you read a run:

- A `fortress compile` of a source that did not change, and whose jar exists, writes nothing and exits 0.
- A library compile that failed or was killed wrote nothing, or only its jar. Programs link the old jar with no warning until you fix the error and compile that component again.

the result of one of the constituent threads that completes abruptly.
After abrupt completion of a group of implicit threads, each reduction
variable (see \secref{reduction-vars})
may reflect an arbitrary subset of updates performed by the
threads in the group.  This means in general that reduction variables
should not be accessed after abrupt completion.  The exact behavior of reduction variables depends on the supporting generator structure and is described in \secref{defining-generators}.

\VAR{T} is the static type of the expression spawned;
this trait has the following methods, each taking no arguments:

\item The \VAR{val} method returns the value computed by the

cd /home/user/fortress-label-exit && export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 PATH=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64/bin:$PATH && export FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD FORTRESS_THREADS=1 TMPDIR=$PWD/tmp JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$PWD/tmp" && unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS; OLD="/home/user/fortress-base35/explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh /home/user/fortress-base35 /home/user/fortress-label-exit/tmp/old-caches"; cd tmp/rung-label-exit/skeptic
cat > SkJ.fss <<'EOF'
component SkJ
export Executable

two(a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32): ZZ32 = a + b

later(k: ZZ32): ZZ32 = two(k, label out
    if k > 0 then exit out with k end
    k + 100
  end out)

run(): () = do
  println("REACHED")
  println("later " || later(5).asString)
end

end
EOF
cat > SkK.fss <<'EOF'
component SkK
export Executable

var log: String = ""

through(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label out
    try
      if n = 1 then exit out with n end
      log := log || "body"
    finally
      log := log || "finally"
    end
    n + 100
  end out

run(): () = do
  a: ZZ32 = through(1)
  println("through(1) " || a.asString || " log [" || log || "]")
  log := ""
  b: ZZ32 = through(2)
  println("through(2) " || b.asString || " log [" || log || "]")
end

end
EOF
cat > SkL.fss <<'EOF'
component SkL
export Executable

sp(n: ZZ32): ZZ32 = label out
    t = spawn do
        if n > 0 then exit out with n end
        n
      end
    t.val() + 100
  end out

run(): () = do
  println("sp " || sp(1).asString)
end

end
EOF
for p in SkJ SkK SkL; do echo "=== $p"; ../../../bin/fortress compile $p.fss > $p.c.txt 2>&1; rc=$?; echo "compile $rc"; grep -v "^\s*at " $p.c.txt | head -c 500; [ $rc = 0 ] && for t in 1 4; do FORTRESS_THREADS=$t ../../../bin/fortress run $p 2>&1 | grep -v "^\s*at " | cut -c1-220 | head -5; done; echo "--- walk"; $OLD $p.fss 2>&1 | grep -v "^\s*at " | cut -c1-220 | head -5; done
